verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              कथं राजा प्रजा रक्षन्नाधिबन्धेन युज्यते। धर्मे च नापराध्नोति तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said You have been told what the duties of a householders are as ordained by the wise. Listen now, O Yudhisthira, to the next class of duties.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              समासेनैव ते राजन्धर्मान्वक्ष्यामि शाश्वतान्। विस्तरेणैव धर्माणां न जात्वन्तमवाप्नुयात्॥२॥
verses.english: Gradually leading off the domestic mode, one should enter the third mode which is good. It is the mode which is followed by persons who living with their wives pain themselves by means of austerities. It is the mode followed by those who live in forest as hermits.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मनिष्ठान् श्रुतवतो वेदव्रतसमाहितान्। अर्चयित्वा यजेथास्त्वं गृहे गुणवतो द्विजान्॥३॥
verses.english: Blessed be you, O son, listen to the duties observed by those who follow this mode of life in which are set forth the practices of all men and all modes of life. Listen, indeed, to the duties of those who live in sacred spots and who have adopted this mode after proper consideration.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्युत्थायोपसंगृह्य चरणावभिवाद्य च। अथ सर्वाणि कुर्वीथाः कार्याणि सपुरोहितः॥४॥
verses.english: Vyasa said When the householder sees his body wrinkled and hair white on his head, and children of his children, he should then retire into the forest.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मकार्याणि निर्वर्त्य मङ्गलानि प्रयुज्य च। ब्राह्मणान्वाचयेथास्त्वमर्थसिद्धिजयाशिषः॥५॥
verses.english: He should pass the third portion of his life as Vanaprastha. He should worship those sacred fires to which he had attended while a householder. Desirous of performing sacrifices, he should also worship the gods.

verses.sanskrit: आर्जवेन च सम्पन्नो धृत्या बुद्ध्या च भारत। यथार्थं प्रतिगृह्णीयात् कामक्रोधौ च वर्जयेत्॥६॥
verses.english: Observing vows and being sparing in diet, he should eat only once, during the sixth part of the day. He should be always careful. Adoring his fires, he should keep some kine, serving them dutifully. He should perform all the rituals of a sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: कामक्रोधौ पुरस्कृत्य योऽर्थं रजाऽनुतिष्ठति। न स धर्मं न चाप्यर्थं प्रतिगृह्णाति बालिशः॥७॥
verses.english: He should live upon rice and wheat which grows indigenously, and upon other sorts of grains, growing wildly. He should eat the remnant after feeding guests. In the third mode of life, he should make offerings of clarified butter in the five celebrated Sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: मा स्म लुब्धांश्च मूर्खांश्च च प्रयूयुजः। अलुब्धान्बुद्धिसम्पन्नान्सर्वकर्मसु योजयेत्॥८॥
verses.english: Four courses of conduct have been laid down for the Vanaprastha mode of life. Some gather only what is necessary for the day. Some store up things for a month.

verses.sanskrit: मूर्खो ह्यधिकृतोऽर्थेषु कार्याणामविशारदः। प्रजाः क्लिश्नात्ययोगेन कामक्रोधसमन्वितः॥९॥
verses.english: Some collect grain and other necessaries sufficient to last for twelve years. Hermits may act thus for adoring guests and performning sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: बलिषष्ठेन शुक्तेन दण्डेनाथापराधिनाम्। शास्त्रानीतेन लिप्सेथा वेतनेन धनागमम्॥१०॥
verses.english: They should during the rains, expose themselves to rain and go to water during the autumn. In summer, they should sit in the midst of four fires with the sun burning overhead. Throughout the year, however, they should be sparing in deit.

verses.sanskrit: दापयित्वा कर धर्म्यं राष्ट्रं नीत्या यथाविधि। तथैतं कल्पयेद्राजा योगक्षेममतन्द्रितः॥११॥
verses.english: They should sit and sleep on the naked earth. They stand on only their toes. They should be satisfied with the bare earth and with small mats of grass. They perform their ablutions morning, noon, and evening.

verses.sanskrit: गोपायितारं दातारं धर्मनित्यमतन्द्रितम्। अकामद्वेषसंयुक्तमनुरज्यन्ति मानवाः॥१२॥
verses.english: Some amongst them use only their teeth for cleaning grain. Others use only stones for the same, Some amongst them drink, only during the light fortnight, boiled very lightly, gruel of wheat (or other, grain).

verses.sanskrit: मा स्मा लोभेनाधर्मेण लिप्सेथास्त्वं धनागमम्। धर्मार्थावध्रुवौ तस्य यो न शास्त्रपरो भवेत्॥१३॥
verses.english: Others drink similar gruel only during the dark fortnight. Some eat what only comes of itself. Some practising rigid vows, live upon only roots, some upon only fruits, some upon only flowers, duly following the method followed by the Vaikhanashas.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थशास्त्रपरो राजा धर्मार्थान्नाधिगच्छति। अस्थाने चास्य तद्वित्तं सर्वमेव विनश्यति॥१४॥
verses.english: These and various other observances are practised by those wise and pious men. The fourth mode of life is based upon the Upanishads. The duties prescribed for it may be observed in all the modes of life equally. Differing from the others this mode comes afler domestic and forest life.

verses.sanskrit: अर्थमूलोऽपि हिंसां च कुरुते स्वयमात्मनः। करैरशास्त्रदृष्टैर्हि मोहात्सम्पीडयन् प्रजाः॥१५॥
verses.english: In this very cycle, O son, many learned Brahmanas knowing the truths of all things, have been known to observe this mode. Agastya, the seven Rishis Madhuchchhandas, Aghamarshana, Sankriti, Sudivatandi who lived with her soever he pleased and was content to take what came (without ever secking for anything), Ahovirya, Kavya, Tandya, the learned medhatithi, the highly energetic Karnanirvaka, and Shunyapala who had worked hard (for acquiring Yoga powel), were the authors of this course of duties, and themselves practising them, have all gone to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: ऊपश्छिन्द्यात्तु यो धेन्वाः क्षीरार्थी न लभेत्पयः। एवं राष्ट्रमयोगेन पीडितं न विवर्धते॥१६॥
verses.english: Many great Rishis, O son, who had the power to see immediately the fruits of their ascetic merit, those numberless ascetics who pass by the appellation of Yayavaras, many Rishis of very austere penances and endued with accurate knowledge about distinctions of duty, and many other Brahınanas too numerous to mention, adopted the forest mode of life. The Vaikhanasas, the Valikhilyas, the Saikatas, all of whom were given to austere penances, who were firm in virtue, who had controlled their senses, and who used to see the fruits of their penances immediately, adopted this mode of life and finally went to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: यो हि दोग्ध्रीमुपास्ते च स नित्यं विन्दते पयः। एवं राष्ट्रमुपायेन भुञ्जानो लभते फलम्॥१७॥
verses.english: Freed from fear and not counted with the stars and planets, these have become visible in the sky as luminaries. When the fourth or last part of life is got at, and when one is weakened by decrepitude and possessed by disease, one should leave off the forest mode of life. Performing a sacrifice capable of being completed in a single day and in which the sacrificial fee should be everything he has, he should himself perforin his own funeral rite. Withdrawn from every other object, he should devote himself to his own self, taking pleasure in himself, and depending also on his own self. He should put up all his sacrificial fires (thenceforth) upon his ownself, and sever all sorts of bonds and attachments.

verses.sanskrit: अथ राष्ट्रमुपायेन भुज्यमानं सुरक्षितम्। जनयत्यतुलां नित्यं कोशवृद्धिं युधिष्ठिर॥१८॥
verses.english: He should always celebrate such sacrifices and rites as are completed in a single day. When, however, from performance of the (ordinary) sacrifices of sacrificers, the Sacrifice in Self begins, then for liberation he should sacrifice his own self in the three fires. Without linding fault with his food he should take five or six mouthfuls, offering them duly to the five vital airs uttering Mantras of the Yajurveda.

verses.sanskrit: दोग्ध्री धान्यं हिरण्यं च मही राज्ञा सुरक्षिता। नित्यं स्वेभ्यः परेभ्यश्च तृप्ता माता यथा पयः॥१९॥
verses.english: Practising austerities while living like a forest recluse, one should shave off and having purified himself by acts, pass into the fourth and the last holy mode of life.

verses.sanskrit: मालाकारोपमो राजन्भव माऽऽङ्गारिकोपमः। तथायुक्तश्चिरं राज्यं भोक्तुं शक्ष्यसि पालयन्॥२०॥
verses.english: That twice-born one who enters the fourth mode of life, giving pledges of assurance to all creatures, succeeds in acquiring many effulgent regions hereafter and ultimately attains to the Infinite.

verses.sanskrit: परचक्राभियानेन यदि ते स्याद्धनक्षयः। अथ साम्नैव लिप्सेथा धनमब्राह्मणेषु यत्॥२१॥
verses.english: Of excellent disposition and conduct, with sins all purged off the person who is conversant with his own self never wished to perform any act for either this or the other world. Shorn of anger, error, anxiety and without friendship, such a person live in this world like one having nothing to do with it.

verses.sanskrit: मा स्म ते ब्राह्मणं दृष्ट्वा धनस्थं प्रचलेन्मनः। अन्त्यायामप्यवस्थायां किमु स्फीतस्य भारत॥२२॥
verses.english: One in the (observance of Sannyasa) should not be unwilling in satisfying the duties included in Yama and those also that walk behind them. Such a person should live energetically according to the ordinances laid down his own mode, and leave off Vedic study and the sacred thread which marks his birth. Given to righteousness and having his senses under complete control, such a person endued with knowledge of self, attains forsooth, to the end for which he tries.

verses.sanskrit: धनानि तेभ्यो दद्यास्त्वं यथाशक्ति यथार्हतः। सान्त्वयन्परिरक्षंश्च स्वर्गमाप्स्यसि दुर्जयम्॥२३॥
verses.english: After the third is the fourth mode of life. It is very superior, and has numberless high virtues. In merit it reigns supreme over the three other modes of life. It is said to occupy the very highest place. Listen to me as I describe the duties belonging to that mode which is very supreme and which is the high refuge of all.

verses.sanskrit: एवं धर्मेण वृत्तेन प्रजास्त्वं परिपालय। स्वन्तं पुण्यं यशो नित्यं प्राप्स्यसे कुरुनन्दन॥२४॥
धर्मेण व्यवहारेण प्रजाः पालय पाण्डव। युधिष्ठिर यथा युक्तो नाधिबन्धेन योक्ष्यसे॥२५॥
verses.english: Protect your subjects piously, O son of Pandu, for you will then suffer no regret or pain.

verses.sanskrit: एष एव परो धर्मो यद्राजा रक्षति प्रजाः। भूतानां हि यथा धर्मो रक्षणं परमा दया॥२६॥
verses.english: Protection of the subject is the greatest duty of the king, since mercy for all creatures and protecting them from injury has been said to be the highest merit.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मादेवं परं धर्मं मन्यन्ते धर्मकोविदाः। यो राजा रक्षणे युक्तो भूतेषु कुरुते दयाम्॥२७॥
verses.english: Persons, conversant with duties, consider that to be the greatest merit of the king, when, engaged in protecting all creatures, he shows mercy towards them.

verses.sanskrit: यदह्ना कुरुते पापमरक्षन्भयतः प्रजाः। राजा वर्षसहस्रेण तस्यान्तमधिगच्छति॥२८॥
verses.english: The sin, a king incurs by neglecting for a single day to protect his subjects from fear, is such that his sufferings are not terminated in hell till after a thousand years.

verses.sanskrit: यदह्ना कुरुते धर्मं प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्। दशवर्षसहस्राणि तस्य भुङ्क्ते फलं दिवि॥२९॥
verses.english: The merit, of a king by protecting his subjects righteously for a single day, is such that he enjoys its reward in heaven for ten thousand years.

verses.sanskrit: स्विष्टिः स्वधीतिः सुतपा लोकाञ्जयति यावतः। क्षणेन तानवाप्नोति प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन्॥३०॥
verses.english: A king, by only protecting his subjects virtuously, soon gains those regions that are acquired by persons leading duly the Garhasthya, the Brahmacharya, and the Vanaprastha modes of life.

verses.sanskrit: एवं धर्मं प्रयत्नेन कौन्तेय परिपालय। ततः पुण्यफलं लब्ध्वा नाधिबन्धेन योक्ष्यसे॥३१॥
verses.english: Do you, O son of Kunti, follow with great care this duty (of protection). You will then obtain the reward of righteousness and suffer no grief and pain. You shall,, O son of Pandu, obtain great prosperity in heaven.

verses.sanskrit: स्वर्गलोके सुमहतीं श्रियं प्राप्स्यसि पाण्डव। असम्भवश्च धर्माणामीदृशानामराजसु॥३२॥
तस्माद्राजैव नान्योऽस्ति यो धर्मफलमाप्नुयात्। स राज्यं धृतिमान्प्राप्य धर्मेण परिपालय। इन्द्रं तर्पय सोमेन कामैश्च सुहृदो जनान्॥३३॥
verses.english: Endued with intelligence, you have obtained a kingdom. Do you protect your subjects righteously. Please Indra with offerings of Soma and your friends and wellwishers with the objects they desire for.'
